summary: Integration test suite for the new auto-publish path is structurally sound. Patch targets correctly switched to news_bot.transcreate_via_claude per Task 7 import convention. outage_state public API used everywhere (no raw SQL on bot_state). All four acceptance scenarios (outage / recovery / container restart / manual-review preemption) covered plus the crash-loop guard. One bug-fix landed in this commit (mock_dt.strptime passthrough + utcnow deprecation). Minor cleanup opportunities only.

findings.title: Dead mock attribute: mock_dt.timezone = dt.timezone
findings.description: news_bot.py imports `timezone` as a top-level name from datetime (line 15: `from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone`). Inside news_bot, `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` resolves `timezone` from the module namespace, NOT from the patched `news_bot.datetime` attribute. So setting `mock_dt.timezone = dt.timezone` has no effect at runtime. Harmless but misleading — a maintainer might believe this line is load-bearing.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `mock_dt.timezone = dt.timezone` line from all 5 occurrences. Or, if kept, comment that it's defensive in case a future refactor changes the datetime import form.

findings.title: Recovery test docstring buries the abstraction leak
findings.description: TestOutageStateIntegration.test_recovery_clears_outage_state_and_sends_switchback_ping calls outage_state.record_recovery_event directly because today's job() does NOT invoke it. The docstring explains this honestly, but the test name suggests an end-to-end recovery — readers may miss the fine print. Suggest renaming or adding a top-of-class TODO link to the future hook so it's visible during code search.
findings.recommendation: Either rename to `test_recovery_hook_clears_state_and_returns_switchback_ping` (more accurate — it tests the hook, not the integration), or add a class-level note pointing at the future job()-recovery integration.

findings.title: Persistence test does not actually exercise a fresh process
findings.description: test_outage_state_persists_across_simulated_restart writes via outage_state setters, opens a sqlite3 connection, closes it, and reads back via the same in-process module. Since outage_state opens a short-lived connection per call (no module-level connection cache), this test mostly proves that two sequential reads from the same process see the same row. A genuine 'restart' simulation would need to flush the module's _DEFAULT_CLIENT cache or similar. The current value of this test is small but non-zero (proves the API works against a fresh sqlite3 connection). Acceptable as-is given that the unit test suite tests the persistence layer more rigorously.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Optionally consider deleting if test_outage_state.py already covers this — it would reduce maintenance surface.
